aciklama: The stories and miracles of the 25 prophets named in the Qur'an, and lessons for life.

kartlar.baslik: 25 Prophets in the Qur'an
kartlar.icerik:
A total of 25 prophets are named in the Qur'an. Belief in all the prophets is the fourth article of iman. A Muslim approaches all the prophets sent by Allah with respect and faith.

"Muhammad... is the last of the prophets." (al-Ahzab 33/40)

The 25 prophets named in the Qur'an:
Adam · Idris · Nuh · Hud · Salih · Ibrahim · Lut · Ismail · Ishaq · Yaqub · Yusuf · Shuayb · Ayyub · Musa · Harun · Dawud · Sulayman · Ilyas · al-Yasa · Dhul-Kifl · Yunus · Zakariya · Yahya · Isa · Muhammad

The 5 great prophets of Ulul-Azm (possessors of determination and patience who bore great responsibility): Nuh · Ibrahim · Musa · Isa · Muhammad (al-Ahqaf 46/35)
kartlar.vurgu: Belief in the 25 prophets · First: Prophet Adam · Last: Prophet Muhammad

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) — The First Human and the First Prophet
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Safiyullah (the servant chosen by Allah)

Allah created Prophet Adam from clay and breathed a soul into him. The angels prostrated to Prophet Adam at Allah's command; this prostration was not worship, but an act of obedience to Allah's command and respect for Prophet Adam. Only Iblis arrogantly refused: "I am superior to him." (al-A'raf 7/12) After Prophet Adam and his wife ate from the forbidden fruit, they were sent down to earth. They repented, saying, "Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves...", and Allah accepted their repentance. (al-A'raf 7/23)

The Qur'an speaks of Prophet Adam's two sons but does not name them. In narrations, the two sons are called Habil and Qabil. Qabil killed his brother out of jealousy, and this event is described as the first murder on earth. (al-Ma'idah 5/27-31)

Miracles: His direct creation by Allah · Being taught all the names
Main lesson: Arrogance is the way of Satan; making mistakes is human, while repentance brings salvation
Main surahs: al-Baqarah (2) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: First human · Created from clay · Forgiven through repentance

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Idris (peace be upon him) — Raised to a High Station
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Siddiq (one who is very truthful) · Prophet

The Qur'an provides information about Prophet Idris in only two passages:
• "He was a truthful prophet, and We raised him to a high station." (Maryam 19/56-57)
• He is mentioned among those who were patient and did good. (al-Anbiya 21/85-86)

Beyond this, the Qur'an contains no detailed account of his story.

Main lesson: Truthfulness and patience lead to high stations with Allah
Note: Scholars hold different views on whether Prophet Idris lived before or after Prophet Nuh. This detail should be learned as information from narrations, not as a certainty.
kartlar.vurgu: Truthful prophet · Raised to a high station (Maryam 19/56)

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) — 950 Years of Patience
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Grateful servant (al-Isra 17/3)

He called his people to the oneness of Allah for 950 years, night and day, openly and in private. (Nuh 71/5-9) Very few believed. He built an ark at Allah's command; his people mocked him. When the flood began, he took a pair of every living creature and the believers aboard the ark.

His son did not believe and drowned. In response to Prophet Nuh's prayer, Allah said: "He is not of your family; he was a doer of evil." (Hud 11/46) The ark came to rest on Mount Judi.

Miracle: Salvation from the flood
Main lesson: Family ties cannot take precedence over iman; 950 years of patience and perseverance
Main surahs: Nuh (71) · Hud (11)
kartlar.vurgu: 950 years of calling his people · His son did not believe · The ark came to rest on Mount Judi

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) — Prophet to the People of Ad
kartlar.icerik:
He was sent to the people of Ad, who built strong, large buildings. He called them to the oneness of Allah; his people arrogantly rejected him.

Allah sent a violent wind upon them without interruption for 7 nights and 8 days; the people were utterly destroyed. (al-Haqqah 69/6-8 · al-Ahqaf 46/21-25)

Hud and the believers were saved.

Main lesson: The people of Ad arrogantly rejected Prophet Hud; Allah sent a wind upon them without interruption for 7 nights and 8 days and utterly destroyed them
Main surahs: Hud (11) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: People of Ad · Wind for 7 nights and 8 days · Arrogance leads to destruction

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) — The Prophet of the She-Camel
kartlar.icerik:
He was sent to the people of Thamud, who carved homes into rocks. The people asked for a miracle; Allah sent a she-camel: "This is Allah's she-camel; do not harm her, and let her drink water." (Hud 11/64)

The defiant among the people slaughtered the she-camel. Prophet Salih warned them: "Enjoy yourselves for three more days, then punishment will come." At the end of the three days, a mighty blast, called a sayha (a devastating, destructive sound), utterly destroyed the people. (ash-Shams 91/11-14)

Miracle: The she-camel sent by Allah's permission
Main lesson: The people of Thamud violated the miracle by slaughtering Allah's she-camel; at the end of three days, the sayha utterly destroyed them
Main surahs: Hud (11) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: People of Thamud · Miracle of the she-camel · Three-day warning

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) — Khalilullah
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Khalilullah (the friend of Allah) · an-Nisa 4/125

In his youth, he broke the idols. He was thrown into a fire; Allah commanded: "O fire! Be cool and safe for Ibrahim." The fire did not burn him. (al-Anbiya 21/68-70) When his father did not believe, he parted from him. After a dream, he prepared to sacrifice his son; his son said, "Do what you are commanded; I will be patient" — Allah sent a ram. (as-Saffat 37/102-107)

He built the Kaaba together with Prophet Ismail. (al-Baqarah 2/127) Allah made him an imam (leader) for humanity and a representative of the hanif faith (the path of belief in Allah's oneness, turning to Him and staying away from associating partners with Him).

Miracles: The fire did not burn him · The resurrection of four birds
Main lesson: Complete submission — being ready to sacrifice everything for Allah, including life and family
Main surahs: Ibrahim (14) · al-Baqarah (2) · as-Saffat (37)
kartlar.vurgu: Khalilullah · The fire did not burn him · Built the Kaaba

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) — The Prophet of Sodom
kartlar.icerik:
Prophet Ibrahim's nephew. He called the people of Sodom both to the oneness of Allah and to moral purification. The Qur'an states that his people committed indecent acts never seen before. (al-A'raf 7/80) His people rejected this warning.

Allah sent angels as guests. The people wanted to harm the angels. At Allah's command, Prophet Lut and the believers left the city at night; however, his wife stayed behind because she did not believe. When morning came, the city was overturned, and stones rained down upon it. (Hud 11/77-83)

Main lesson: The people of Sodom did not believe; the city was overturned in the morning and stones rained down upon it — Prophet Lut's wife was also not saved because she did not believe
Main surahs: Hud (11) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: Prophet Ibrahim's nephew · Sodom was destroyed · His wife did not believe

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Ismail (peace be upon him) — Sadiq al-Wa'd
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Sadiq al-Wa'd (faithful to his promise) · Maryam 19/54

The elder son of Prophet Ibrahim. He was left with his mother Hajar in the waterless desert of the valley of Makkah. The emergence of the water of Zamzam is not mentioned by name in the Quran; it is found in authentic narrations about our mother Hajar's efforts. (Bukhari, Anbiya 9)

When his father wanted to sacrifice him, he said: "Do as you are commanded, my father! If Allah wills, you will find me among the patient." (as-Saffat 37/102) Allah saw this submission and sent a ram. He built the Kaaba with his father Ibrahim. (al-Baqarah 2/127)

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was a descendant of Prophet Ismail.

Main lesson: Complete submission and keeping one's word
Main surahs: al-Baqarah (2) · as-Saffat (37)
kartlar.vurgu: Sadiq al-Wa'd · The test of sacrifice · Helped build the Kaaba

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Ishaq (peace be upon him) — The Prophet Whose Birth Was Glad Tidings
kartlar.icerik:
The second son of Prophet Ibrahim and the brother of Prophet Ismail. Glad tidings were given that he would be born to a very elderly mother (Sarah) and father.

When the angels came to Prophet Ibrahim, Sarah said, "I am an old woman, and my husband is elderly too—this is an amazing thing!" The angels said: "Such is Allah's command." (Hud 11/72)

Prophet Ishaq was the father of Prophet Yaqub, and Prophet Yaqub had 12 sons (the ancestors of the Children of Israel). The line of prophethood continued.

Miracle: His birth to elderly and barren parents
Main lesson: Nothing is impossible for Allah
Main surahs: Hud (11) · as-Saffat (37)
kartlar.vurgu: Born to elderly parents · Father of Prophet Yaqub

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Yaqub (peace be upon him) — Israel
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Israel (servant of Allah) · Son of Prophet Ishaq

His sons were jealous of Prophet Yusuf, threw him into a well, and brought back his bloodstained shirt. Prophet Yaqub said: "Your souls have led you to do something. Beautiful patience is needed." (Yusuf 12/18) His eyes turned white from grief.

Years later, he sensed Yusuf's scent from afar. When his sons brought the shirt, his sight returned. (Yusuf 12/94–96) He went to Egypt and was reunited with his son; Yusuf's childhood dream came true.

His 12 sons are the ancestors of the Children of Israel.

Main lesson: Beautiful patience (sabr jamil) — never losing hope in Allah
Main surah: Yusuf (12)
kartlar.vurgu: Known as Israel · Longed for Yusuf · Beautiful patience

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) — The Most Beautiful of Stories
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Siddiq (most truthful) · "The most beautiful of stories" (Yusuf 12/3)

His brothers threw him into a well → he was sold into slavery in Egypt → he did not fall into the trap of the woman described in the Quran as the wife of the Aziz and called Zulaykha in narrations → he was thrown into prison → he interpreted the dream of the ruler of Egypt (7 years of abundance, 7 years of famine) → he became a trusted administrator in charge of the country's storehouses.

He recognized his brothers when they came during the famine but did not reveal who he was; finally, he told them: "I am Yusuf. There is no blame upon you today; may Allah forgive you." (Yusuf 12/90–92) When his father came, his childhood dream came true.

Miracle: Interpretation of dreams · Allah clearing him of blame
Main lesson: Patience and chastity; not responding to evil with evil
Main surah: Yusuf (12) — in its entirety
kartlar.vurgu: The most beautiful of stories · Chastity and patience · He forgave his brothers

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Shuayb (peace be upon him) — The Prophet of Business Ethics
kartlar.icerik:
He was sent to the people of Madyan. Some narrations say that Prophet Shuayb was the righteous man for whom Prophet Musa worked in Madyan; the Quran does not explicitly name this man.

His people cheated in trade, giving short measure and weight. "Give full measure and weight, and do not deprive people of what is theirs." (Hud 11/85) When his people rejected him, a cloud offering shade came over them—they hoped for coolness but met with punishment; a mighty blast destroyed them.

When Prophet Musa fled to Madyan, he married the daughter of a righteous man and worked as a shepherd for years. In narrations, this man is most often identified as Prophet Shuayb.

Main lesson: Business ethics are not separate from worship; earning a halal livelihood is an act of worship
Main surahs: Hud (11) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: The people of Madyan · Fairness in weights and measures · The connection to Prophet Musa is mentioned in narrations

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) — The Pinnacle of Patience
kartlar.icerik:
Title: "What an excellent servant! Indeed, he constantly turned to Allah." (Sad 38/44)

He was tested with a serious illness for years—he lost his wealth, his children, and his health. But he did not complain; he turned to Allah in submission.

He prayed: "My Lord! Harm has afflicted me, and You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy." (al-Anbiya 21/83) Allah accepted his prayer, removed his illness, and restored his family to him and gave him more besides.

Miracle: His healing
Main lesson: Turning to Allah even in the hardest trial; maintaining patience, prayer, and hope in the face of hardship
Main surahs: al-Anbiya (21) · Sad (38)
kartlar.vurgu: Years of illness · He did not complain · He was healed through his prayer

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) — Kalimullah
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Kalimullah (the one who spoke with Allah) · The prophet mentioned most often in the Quran (136 times)

During Pharaoh's reign, he was placed in a chest and set afloat on the Nile, and he grew up in the palace. He spoke with Allah at Sinai. He was sent to Pharaoh. Nine miracles were shown: the staff, the white hand, the flood, locusts, vermin (harmful insects), frogs, blood, famine, and a decrease in fruits. Pharaoh denied them every time.

He parted the sea with his staff; the Children of Israel crossed, and Pharaoh drowned. He spoke with Allah at Sinai for 40 nights; he was given the Torah.

Miracles: The staff turning into a snake · The parting of the sea · Speaking directly with Allah
Main lesson: Pharaoh arrogantly rejected all the miracles; he pursued the Children of Israel into the sea and drowned — Allah raises whomever He wills from wherever He wills
Main surahs: Ta-Ha (20) · al-Qasas (28) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: Kalimullah · Mentioned 136 times · Parted the sea · Given the Torah

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Harun (peace be upon him) — Musa's Helper
kartlar.icerik:
The elder brother of Prophet Musa. Prophet Musa prayed to Allah: "Make my brother Harun my helper and increase my strength." (Ta-Ha 20/29–32) Allah accepted his prayer, and Prophet Harun was also appointed as a prophet.

While Prophet Musa was at Sinai, the people worshipped the golden calf. Prophet Harun tried to stop them: "O my people! You have been tested by this." But the people did not listen. (Ta-Ha 20/90–94) When Musa returned, Harun said, "They did not listen to me; they nearly killed me."

Main lesson: Helping one another brings strength; even a leader cannot always restrain his people — responsibility is individual
Main surahs: Ta-Ha (20) · al-A'raf (7)
kartlar.vurgu: Musa's helper · Could not prevent the worship of the calf

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) — Khalifatullah
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Khalifatullah (the servant whom Allah entrusted with the duty of ruling justly on earth) · Sad 38/26

While he was a young shepherd, he defeated and killed Goliath with his sling. Allah gave him dominion (rule), wisdom (deep understanding), and the Zabur. (al-Baqarah 2/251)

The mountains and birds glorified Allah with him. (Sad 38/18-20) Allah softened iron for him and taught him to make armor. (al-Anbiya 21/80) "O Dawud! We have made you a vicegerent on earth, so judge between people with justice." (Sad 38/26)

Miracles: The mountains and birds glorifying Allah · The softening of iron · The Zabur
Main lesson: Power is a gift from Allah; ruling justly is the greatest trust
Main surahs: Sad (38) · al-Anbiya (21)
kartlar.vurgu: Khalifatullah · Given the Zabur · Iron was softened for him

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) — Ruler over the Jinn and the Wind
kartlar.icerik:
The son of Prophet Dawud. Allah subjected the wind, the jinn, and the language of birds to him (placed them at his command). (an-Naml 27/17 · Saba 34/12)

The hoopoe reported that the queen of Saba and her people worshipped the sun. The Quran does not name this queen; she is called Bilqis in narrations. Prophet Sulayman wrote her a letter inviting her to Allah. Her throne was brought "in the blink of an eye." The queen mistook the crystal floor for water; when she understood the truth, she said, "I have submitted with Sulayman to the Lord of the worlds," and believed. (an-Naml 27/44)

Prophet Sulayman died while leaning on his staff; the jinn did not realize it until they saw the worm gnawing at the staff. This event shows that only Allah knows the unseen (hidden knowledge that cannot be perceived by the senses).

Main lesson: Great blessings require great gratitude; only Allah knows the unseen
Main surahs: an-Naml (27) · Sad (38)
kartlar.vurgu: Ruled over the wind and the jinn · The queen of Saba believed · Allah knows the unseen

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Ilyas (peace be upon him) — He Who Stood against the Idol Ba'l
kartlar.icerik:
He was sent to the Children of Israel. He opposed his people's worship of an idol named Ba'l: "Do you worship Ba'l and abandon the best of creators? Fear Allah, your Lord." (as-Saffat 37/124-126)

His people denied him. Allah mentioned him among those who do good and the chosen, and greeted him with peace.

His name appears 3 times in the Quran: al-An'am 6/85, as-Saffat 37/123 and 37/130.

Main lesson: Standing against idolatry is a shared duty of the prophets
Main surah: as-Saffat (37)
kartlar.vurgu: Sent to the Children of Israel · Opposed the idol Ba'l · Allah greeted him with peace

kartlar.baslik: Prophet al-Yasa (peace be upon him) — Among the Chosen
kartlar.icerik:
The Quran mentions Prophet al-Yasa in only two verses:
• al-An'am 6/86: Among the prophets descended from Ibrahim
• Sad 38/48: Among the righteous

"We counted all of them among the righteous." (Sad 38/48)

Beyond this, no detailed account of his story is given in the Quran. It is narrated that he lived around the time of Prophet Ilyas.

Main lesson: Belief in all prophets is essential, even if their stories are brief
Main surahs: al-An'am (6) · Sad (38)
kartlar.vurgu: Mentioned in two verses · Mentioned among the righteous

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) — Dhun-Nun
kartlar.icerik:
Titles: Dhun-Nun (the one associated with the fish) · Sahib-ul Hut (the person associated with the fish)

He called his people to Allah in Nineveh. He left his people without Allah's permission. Lots were drawn on the ship, and he was thrown into the sea. A large fish swallowed him.

He prayed in the darkness: "La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin" (There is no deity but You; I declare You free from imperfection; I have truly been among those who wronged themselves). (al-Anbiya 21/87) Allah accepted his prayer; the fish left him on the shore.

His people also repented—they are mentioned as the only people who believed upon seeing the punishment and whose repentance was accepted. (Yunus 10/98)

Miracle: Surviving in the belly of the fish
Main lesson: Prayer brings deliverance at the darkest moment; one must not leave a duty without Allah's permission
Main surahs: Yunus (10) · as-Saffat (37)
kartlar.vurgu: Dhun-Nun · Prayed in the belly of the fish · His people repented and were saved

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Zakariyya (peace be upon him) — He Never Stopped Asking Allah
kartlar.icerik:
Whenever he visited Maryam in the sanctuary, he found food with her. "Where does this come to you from?" "From Allah." (Al Imran 3/37) He then asked Allah for a child:

"My Lord! My bones have weakened, my hair has turned white, and my wife was barren. Grant me an heir from Yourself." (Maryam 19/4-6) Allah said: "We give you the good news of Yahya; We have given this name to no one before." (Maryam 19/7)

Miracle: The birth of Prophet Yahya to his elderly and barren wife
Main lesson: Never stop asking Allah; a private prayer is a sign of sincerity
Main surahs: Maryam (19) · Al Imran (3)
kartlar.vurgu: Inspired by Maryam · Prophet Yahya was born to his barren wife

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Yahya (peace be upon him) — Given Wisdom as a Child
kartlar.icerik:
The son of Prophet Zakariyya. He was born to elderly and barren parents.

"O Yahya! Hold fast to the Scripture. We gave him wisdom as a child." (Maryam 19/12) He was compassionate toward people, kept away from sins, respected his parents, and was neither tyrannical nor rebellious. (Maryam 19/13-14)

He was a contemporary of Prophet Isa. His name had never been given to anyone before. (Maryam 19/7)

Miracles: Receiving wisdom as a child · The uniqueness of his name
Main lesson: Wisdom does not depend on age; respect for parents is a shared quality of the prophets
Main surahs: Maryam (19) · Al Imran (3)
kartlar.vurgu: Given wisdom as a child · His name was used for the first time

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Dhul-Kifl (peace be upon him) — Among the Patient
kartlar.icerik:
The Quran mentions Prophet Dhul-Kifl in only two verses:
• al-Anbiya 21/85-86: Among the patient, alongside Prophets Ismail and Idris
• Sad 38/48: Among the righteous

Beyond this, there is no detailed account of his story in the Quran.

Important note: Prophet Dhul-Kifl is counted among the 25 prophets named in the Quran. Most scholars regard him as a prophet; some scholars have said that he may have been a righteous ruler. Therefore, rather than speaking with certainty about the details, it is enough to know that the Quran mentions him for his patience and goodness.

Main lesson: Belief in all prophets is essential; even if their stories are brief, their standing with Allah is great
kartlar.vurgu: Mentioned in two verses · Remembered for patience and goodness

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) — Ruhullah and Kalimatullah
kartlar.icerik:
Titles: Ruhullah (one described as a spirit from Allah) and Kalimatullah (created by Allah's command “Be”) · Aal Imran 3/45

He was born to Mary without a father: “We said, ‘Be,’ and it was.” (Aal Imran 3/47) He spoke in the cradle: “I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.” (Maryam 19/30) By Allah's permission, he made a bird from clay and breathed into it (and it flew), healed the blind and those with leprosy, raised the dead, and brought down a table spread with food from heaven. (Aal Imran 3/49)

The Jews wanted to kill him; Allah said, “I will raise you to Myself.” (an-Nisa 4/157–158)

The Quran clearly states: Prophet Isa is Allah's servant, not Allah's son. (an-Nisa 4/171)

Miracles: Birth without a father · Speaking in the cradle · Raising the dead · A table spread with food from heaven
Main surahs: Maryam (19) · Aal Imran (3)
kartlar.vurgu: Ruhullah · Born without a father · Spoke in the cradle · Allah's servant

kartlar.baslik: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ — The Last Prophet
kartlar.icerik:
Title: Khatam al-Anbiya (Seal of the Prophets, meaning the last prophet)

“Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets.” (al-Ahzab 33/40)

The name “Muhammad” appears 4 times in the Quran: Aal Imran 3/144, al-Ahzab 33/40, Muhammad 47/2, al-Fath 48/29. He is also mentioned once by the name “Ahmad” (as-Saff 61/6 — the glad tidings given by Prophet Isa).

His miracles: The Noble Quran (the greatest and everlasting miracle) · Isra and Mi'raj (the Night Journey and ascent to exalted stations) · The splitting of the moon

Main lesson: He is the last prophet — no prophet will come after him; the Quran will be preserved until the Day of Judgment

Note: See the Sirah section for a detailed account of his life.
kartlar.vurgu: The last prophet · The Quran is his greatest miracle · Details in the Sirah section

kartlar.baslik: Differences Between Schools of Thought and Important Notes
kartlar.icerik:
Some important points about the stories of the prophets:

• Total number of prophets: Some hadith narrations mention that 124,000 prophets were sent. Only 25 names appear in the Quran; no details are given about the others. Therefore, the names we know with certainty are those mentioned in the Quran.

• Ulul-Azm prophets: The 5 great prophets distinguished by their resolve and patience: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. (al-Ahqaf 46/35)

• Isra'iliyyat: Information that entered the stories of the prophets from the Torah and Jewish and Christian narrations is called “Isra'iliyyat.” Details not found in the Quran (e.g., the names Habil and Qabil, the name Bilqis, and certain historical details) are approached with caution; if there is no verse confirming or contradicting them, they are described as “it is narrated.”

• Prophet Dhul-Kifl: Most scholars consider him a prophet; some scholars have said that he may have been a righteous ruler. The Quran mentions him among the patient and righteous servants.
